cohort: The study included 446 women who underwent planned oocyte cryopreservation at a university-affiliated medical center between 2011 and 2018, with 57 of these women later attempting to use their cryopreserved oocytes.
finding: Women who underwent planned oocyte cryopreservation at age 40 and older had a low live birth success rate, and oocyte shipping to ancillary sites was associated with a lower survival rate after thawing.
followup_time: up to 10 years (from 2011 to June 2021) after oocyte cryopreservation for utilization and live birth outcomes
